Guideline: Version every QML import
Description: Qt 5 requires version numbers on QML imports; unversioned imports fail or resolve unpredictably.
Do: Write the major.minor version on every import (QtQuick 2.15, Controls 2.15, Layouts 1.15).
Don't: Omit version numbers (a Qt 6 habit) in Qt 5 code.
Code Good: import QtQuick 2.15; import QtQuick.Controls 2.15; import QtQuick.Layouts 1.15
Code Bad: import QtQuick; import QtQuick.Controls

Guideline: Use the plain Controls import unless a file customizes controls
Description: A style-specific import (e.g. QtQuick.Controls.Material) is compile-time style selection: it overrides run-time style selection for that file, so the app can no longer be re-themed via QT_QUICK_CONTROLS_STYLE or qtquickcontrols2.conf.
Do: Keep the plain import in files that do not override background/contentItem/indicator/handle; add the style-specific import only in the customizing files.
Don't: Add a style-specific import app-wide just because one file needs it.
Code Bad: import QtQuick.Controls.Material 2.15  // in every file, kills run-time theming

Guideline: Prefer Qt Quick Controls over hand-built primitives
Description: Controls 2 buttons, fields and dialogs already carry focus, keyboard, touch and accessibility behavior; rebuilding them from Rectangle + MouseArea re-implements all of it badly.
Do: Use Button, TextField, Dialog and other Controls 2 types for interactive elements.
Don't: Build buttons from Rectangle + MouseArea + Text for normal app UI.
Code Bad: Rectangle { MouseArea { onClicked: save() } Text { text: "Save" } }

Guideline: Register QML modules with qmldir in Qt 5, not qt_add_qml_module
Description: qt_add_qml_module is a Qt 6 CMake API. Qt 5 projects expose reusable QML with a qmldir file (qmake) or a CMake qml module via qt5_add_resources / manual qmldir install.
Do: Ship a qmldir next to the QML files and add it to the .qrc or install step.
Don't: Copy Qt 6 qt_add_qml_module blocks into a Qt 5 build.
Code Good: module App.Controls  // qmldir + QML files installed together
Code Bad: qt_add_qml_module(app_controls URI App.Controls VERSION 1.0)

Guideline: Keep style selection in one place
Description: Scattered style imports and per-file style overrides make the app impossible to re-theme for a customer or a dark variant.
Do: Select the style once (qtquickcontrols2.conf, QT_QUICK_CONTROLS_STYLE, or one style import in the customizing files) and keep tokens in a singleton.
Don't: Mix Material in one file, Universal in another, and hardcoded colors in a third.
Code Good: Material.theme: Material.Dark  // set once, tokens referenced everywhere
Code Bad: Button { background: Rectangle { color: "#2563eb" } }  // hardcoded per file

Guideline: main.qml is a bootstrap file only
Description: The root file declares the window and wires top-level screens/navigation. Business logic, deep item trees, inline delegates and dialogs make it unreviewable.
Do: Keep main.qml shallow; move screens, panels, dialogs and delegates to their own files.
Don't: Grow main.qml into a multi-hundred-line tree with inline delegates and dialogs.
Code Bad: ApplicationWindow { /* 400 lines: dialogs, delegates, logic inline */ }

Guideline: Extract a component on reuse, on responsibility, or on depth
Description: Any object literal used twice, any screen/panel/dialog/toolbar/delegate, or any tree deeper than ~3 levels or ~150-200 lines deserves its own PascalCase file.
Do: Split at those thresholds; name the file after the type.
Don't: Keep duplicating the same card/delegate literal across screens.
Code Good: // Card.qml, SettingsPanel.qml, UserDelegate.qml — one type per file
Code Bad: // same 40-line card literal pasted into three screens

Guideline: One screen, one task on embedded targets
Description: Fixed-resolution embedded screens with overlapping panels and deep navigation confuse users and cost memory; flat navigation (max 2 levels) and one task per screen fit the hardware.
Do: Design one task per screen and keep navigation flat and always visible.
Don't: Stack panels, drawers and dialogs over each other on a small fixed screen.
Code Good: StackView { /* Home -> Detail, back always visible */ }
Code Bad: /* drawer over dialog over panel, back path unclear */

Guideline: Never create a binding loop
Description: If A depends on B and B depends on A, the engine warns and one value flickers or sticks; loops in delegates multiply the cost.
Do: Break one link with an explicit source of truth (a property both sides read).
Don't: Bind width to content and content width back to the container width.
Code Good: readonly property real cellW: listView.width / columns  // one direction
Code Bad: item.width: content.width; content.width: item.width  // loop

Guideline: Prefer declarative bindings over imperative assignment
Description: Assigning a value in JS (prop = value) permanently destroys any binding on that property; later source changes stop propagating and the bug is silent.
Do: Write prop: expression; if an imperative override is ever needed, restore with Qt.binding().
Don't: Set bound properties from event handlers with plain assignment.
Code Bad: onEnabledChanged: item.opacity = enabled ? 1 : 0.4  // kills binding

Guideline: Keep hot bindings cheap: cache in a readonly property
Description: A function call inside a binding re-runs on every dependency change; in delegates that cost multiplies by item count.
Do: Compute once into a readonly property and bind to that.
Don't: Call formatting or lookup functions directly inside delegate bindings.
Code Good: readonly property string priceText: fmt(price)  // then text: priceText
Code Bad: text: fmt(model.price) + " " + lookup(model.code)  // per frame per item

Guideline: Guard expensive bindings with Binding { when }
Description: Bindings that poll hardware, sensors or large models cost CPU even when their screen is hidden.
Do: Wrap costly bindings in Binding { when: visible } so they deactivate off-screen.
Don't: Leave sensor-driven bindings live for hidden screens.
Code Good: Binding { target: gauge; property: "value"; value: sensor.value; when: gauge.visible }
Code Bad: value: sensor.value  // always live, even when hidden

Guideline: Use explicit ids, never implicit dynamic scope
Description: QML resolves bare names by walking the scope chain; an added intermediate id can silently rebind a reference to the wrong object.
Do: Reference cross-component objects by explicit id.
Don't: Rely on a bare name resolving to a distant ancestor's property.
Code Bad: onClicked: save()  // resolves wherever scope happens to find it

Guideline: Never mix anchors and Layout.* on the same item
Description: Anchors and layout attached properties fight over geometry; the result is unpredictable sizing and warnings.
Do: Pick one system per item: anchors for free placement, Layout.* inside RowLayout/ColumnLayout/GridLayout.
Don't: Set both anchors.left and Layout.fillWidth on the same item.
Code Bad: RowLayout { Button { anchors.left: parent.left; Layout.fillWidth: true } }

Guideline: Size layout-managed items with Layout.* only
Description: Setting width/height directly on an item whose parent is a Layout is ignored by the layout's size negotiation, so the item silently sizes wrong.
Do: Use Layout.preferredWidth, Layout.fillWidth, Layout.minimumHeight and friends for children of layouts, at every nesting level.
Don't: Set width: 200 on a child of RowLayout and wonder why it is ignored.
Code Bad: ColumnLayout { Button { width: 200 } }  // ignored by the layout

Guideline: Prefer anchors.fill over four separate edges
Description: Four edge anchors are verbose and easy to get inconsistent; anchors.fill expresses the same intent in one line.
Do: Use anchors.fill: parent with anchors.margins for full-bleed children.
Don't: Write anchors.top/left/right/bottom separately for a fill.
Code Bad: Rectangle { anchors.top: parent.top; anchors.left: parent.left; anchors.right: parent.right; anchors.bottom: parent.bottom }

Guideline: Never anchor to invisible items
Description: Anchoring to a visible: false item collapses the anchor target unpredictably and shifts siblings.
Do: Anchor to a visible container, or collapse the hidden item's space explicitly with a Layout/visible guard.
Don't: Anchor a label's top to a hidden header and ship the shifted layout.
Code Good: Column { Header { visible: showHeader } Body { } }  // space follows visibility
Code Bad: Body { anchors.top: hiddenHeader.bottom }  // hiddenHeader.visible: false

Guideline: Use Row/Column for static lists, Layouts for responsive ones
Description: Row/Column are lighter than RowLayout/ColumnLayout; layouts pay for size negotiation that static arrangements never need.
Do: Use Row/Column for uniform static arrangements and Layouts when resizing must redistribute space.
Don't: Wrap every static icon row in a RowLayout.
Code Bad: RowLayout { spacing: 8; Icon {}; Icon {} }  // pays layout cost for nothing

Guideline: Drive control appearance from the style, not per-control colors
Description: Hardcoded background colors per control defeat theming: a dark variant or customer skin then needs every file touched.
Do: Use the active style (Material/Universal/Fusion) and its attached properties; override background/contentItem only in the dedicated customizing files.
Don't: Set background: Rectangle { color: ... } on every button.
Code Bad: Button { background: Rectangle { color: "#2563eb" } }  // per control

Guideline: Keep control sizes implicit; pad, don't hardcode
Description: Hardcoded widths break translated text (30-40% longer than English) and large-font modes; implicit sizes plus padding absorb both.
Do: Let implicitWidth/implicitHeight drive size and use padding for touch area.
Don't: Set width: 80 on a button whose label will be translated.
Code Good: Button { padding: 12; text: qsTr("Save") }  // grows with text
Code Bad: Button { width: 80; text: qsTr("Save") }  // clips translated text

Guideline: One primary action per group; demote the rest
Description: Two equally loud buttons force a choice the user should not have to make; OK + Cancel is one group, anything else is secondary.
Do: Style one primary action per group and make the rest flat/secondary.
Don't: Render Save, Delete and Cancel all as highlighted buttons.
Code Good: Row { Button { highlighted: true; text: qsTr("Save") } Button { flat: true; text: qsTr("Cancel") } }
Code Bad: Row { Button { highlighted: true; text: qsTr("Save") } Button { highlighted: true; text: qsTr("Delete") } }

Guideline: Show a visible focus indicator on every custom control
Description: Keyboard users are lost without a focus ring; built-in Controls draw one, hand-built items do not.
Do: Bind a border or scale to activeFocus on custom interactive items, and set activeFocusOnTab: true.
Don't: Ship a custom control with no focus visual at all.
Code Good: Rectangle { border.color: activeFocus ? Theme.accent : "transparent"; activeFocusOnTab: true }
Code Bad: Rectangle { /* no focus visual, no activeFocusOnTab */ }

Guideline: Confirm before destructive or irreversible actions
Description: A destructive tap with no confirmation cannot be undone on embedded hardware; dialogs are cheap insurance.
Do: Gate delete, reset and actuator commands behind a confirmation dialog.
Don't: Delete records or drive an actuator on a single unguarded tap.
Code Good: Button { onClicked: confirmDialog.open() }  // Dialog confirms first
Code Bad: Button { onClicked: backend.eraseAll() }  // no confirmation

Guideline: Keep system state permanently visible on embedded screens
Description: On a panel, connected/error/active-mode state hidden behind a tooltip or hover does not exist; the operator must see it at a glance.
Do: Reserve always-visible status area for connection, error and mode state, driven by application state (not transient UI state).
Don't: Show error state only as a transient toast that disappears.
Code Good: StatusBar { /* connection + mode + error, always on screen */ }
Code Bad: /* error shown only in a 3-second toast */

Guideline: Use states for discrete configurations only
Description: States describe named configurations (active, disabled, editing); using them for continuous animation produces state churn and surprise transitions.
Do: Model discrete modes as states and continuous motion as animations.
Don't: Drive a progress sweep by flipping states every frame.
Code Good: states: [ State { name: "editing"; PropertyChanges { target: field; readOnly: false } } ]
Code Bad: states: [ State { name: "p37" } State { name: "p38" } /* ... per frame */ ]

Guideline: In Qt 5, PropertyChanges needs its target
Description: Qt 6 dropped target from PropertyChanges; in Qt 5 the target property is correct and required for the change to apply to the right object.
Do: Write PropertyChanges { target: id; property: value } in Qt 5 code.
Don't: Copy Qt 6 PropertyChanges without target into Qt 5 code.
Code Good: PropertyChanges { target: field; width: 120 }  // Qt 5 correct
Code Bad: PropertyChanges { width: 120 }  // Qt 6 style, wrong target in Qt 5

Guideline: Target transitions with from/to
Description: Catch-all transitions fire on every state change, including ones they were never designed for, producing odd mid-flight visuals.
Do: Write Transition { from: "idle"; to: "editing"; ... } for each intended path.
Don't: Write one bare Transition {} and let it fire on all state changes.
Code Good: Transition { from: "idle"; to: "editing"; NumberAnimation { properties: "opacity"; duration: 200 } }
Code Bad: Transition { NumberAnimation { properties: "opacity"; duration: 200 } }  // fires everywhere

Guideline: Name states as enum-like strings
Description: Free-form state names (s1, temp, foo) make state logic unreadable and ungreppable.
Do: Use stable enum-like names: active, disabled, editing, error.
Don't: Name states s1, temp or foo.
Code Bad: states: [ State { name: "s2" } ]

Guideline: Stop animations when their item is off-screen
Description: Animations tick every frame even when invisible; a hidden screen full of running animations burns CPU on embedded hardware for nothing.
Do: Bind running/paused to effective visibility, or destroy the animated subtree with a Loader.
Don't: Leave animations running on hidden screens.
Code Bad: NumberAnimation { running: true }  // ticks forever, hidden or not

Guideline: Animate transform and opacity, not geometry
Description: Animating width/height/anchors triggers a full relayout every frame; transform and opacity are GPU-composited and cheap.
Do: Animate scale, rotation, x, y and opacity; use Animator types (OpacityAnimator, ScaleAnimator, XAnimator) where supported.
Don't: Animate width on a complex subtree to fake a slide.
Code Good: XAnimator { target: panel; from: -200; to: 0; duration: 250 }
Code Bad: NumberAnimation { target: panel; property: "width"; from: 0; to: 200 }

Guideline: Keep animation budgets: 100-400 ms, one or two at a time
Description: Motion must communicate state, not decorate: small elements 100-150 ms, panels 200-300 ms, full-screen transitions 300-400 ms, never over 500 ms; a whole screen animating at once disorients.
Do: Budget durations by element size and animate at most one or two elements simultaneously.
Don't: Run 800 ms full-screen animation on every navigation.
Code Bad: NumberAnimation { duration: 900 }  // full-screen, feels broken

Guideline: On embedded targets, opacity-only and under 200 ms
Description: Software rasterisation without a GPU makes move-plus-fade and long animations visibly janky; opacity-only transitions under 200 ms stay smooth.
Do: Use opacity-only transitions under 200 ms on GPU-less panels; relax only when a GPU is confirmed.
Don't: Run simultaneous move + fade over 400 ms on a software-rendered panel.
Code Bad: NumberAnimation { properties: "x,opacity"; duration: 400 }  // jank on soft raster

Guideline: Prefer explicit transitions over Behavior on everything
Description: Behavior on x fires on every change including programmatic ones, so a layout correction animates when it should snap.
Do: Use explicit Transition or Animation where you need control over when motion triggers.
Don't: Put Behavior on x on a panel that is also positioned programmatically.
Code Bad: Behavior on x { NumberAnimation { duration: 200 } }  // fires on every set

Guideline: Access model roles as model.roleName
Description: Bare role names in delegates resolve through dynamic scope and can be shadowed by local properties; model.roleName is explicit and stable.
Do: Write model.name, model.price in delegates instead of bare name/price.
Don't: Rely on bare role names that a local property can shadow.
Code Bad: Text { text: name }  // shadowable by a local property

Guideline: Keep delegates minimal
Description: Delegate complexity multiplies by item count; a heavy delegate turns a 100-row list into 100 heavy trees.
Do: Put only the row's visuals in the delegate; move detail views, dialogs and heavy logic out.
Don't: Build a full detail editor inside every list delegate.
Code Good: delegate: Row { Text { text: model.name } }  // minimal
Code Bad: delegate: Column { /* editor, charts, dialogs per row */ }

Guideline: In Qt 5, do not use required properties or reuseItems
Description: required properties and ListView.reuseItems are Qt 6 APIs (reuseItems needs 6.7+); they do not exist in Qt 5.15 and break the build.
Do: Use plain delegate properties and model.roleName access in Qt 5; keep delegates cheap instead of relying on pooling.
Don't: Copy Qt 6 delegate code with required property or reuseItems into Qt 5.
Code Good: delegate: Text { text: model.name }  // Qt 5 delegate
Code Bad: ListView { reuseItems: true; delegate: Item { required property string name } }

Guideline: Prefer Repeater + Column for static lists
Description: A ListView pays for scrolling, recycling and viewport bookkeeping that a short static list never uses.
Do: Use Repeater + Column (or Row) for fixed short lists; reserve ListView for scrollable data.
Don't: Use a ListView for a fixed 4-item menu.
Code Good: Column { Repeater { model: 4; delegate: MenuItem {} } }  // static
Code Bad: ListView { model: 4; delegate: MenuItem {} }  // scrolling machinery unused

Guideline: Remember parent in a delegate is not the ListView
Description: Inside a delegate, parent is the delegate's internal visual container; sizing or anchoring to it as if it were the list breaks layout.
Do: Use ListView.view or an explicit list id when the delegate needs the list itself.
Don't: Anchor a delegate child to parent expecting the ListView.
Code Bad: width: parent.width  // parent is the delegate container, not the list

Guideline: Use Loader for conditional UI and set active: false when unused
Description: Loader owns cleanup: deactivating it destroys the component and frees memory, which matters on constrained devices.
Do: Wrap dialogs, popups and optional panels in Loader and drive active from visibility.
Don't: Keep every optional panel instantiated and hidden with visible: false.
Code Bad: SettingsPanel { visible: showSettings }  // instantiated and resident

Guideline: Guard Loader.item access with status === Loader.Ready
Description: Loader.item is null until the component finishes loading; touching it early crashes or silently no-ops.
Do: Access item only after status === Loader.Ready (or in onLoaded).
Don't: Read loader.item.width immediately after setting source.
Code Bad: loader.item.focus = true  // item may be null

Guideline: Load heavy components asynchronously
Description: Synchronous loading blocks the UI thread and drops frames on first open of a heavy panel.
Do: Set Loader.asynchronous: true for heavy components.
Don't: Synchronously load a chart-heavy panel on first tap.
Code Bad: Loader { sourceComponent: chartPanel }  // blocks UI thread

Guideline: Prefer inline Component over Qt.createComponent URL strings
Description: URL-string dynamic creation bypasses compile-time checks and scatters component identity across strings.
Do: Define inline Component {} blocks and instantiate with createObject only when the parent is genuinely dynamic; otherwise use Loader.
Don't: Create components from URL strings scattered through code.
Code Bad: Qt.createComponent("Row.qml")  // stringly-typed

Guideline: Register C++ types with qmlRegisterType in Qt 5
Description: Qt 5 exposes C++ to QML with qmlRegisterType (and qmlRegisterSingletonType); the Qt 6 QML_ELEMENT macro does not exist in Qt 5.
Do: Register with qmlRegisterType<Backend>("App", 1, 0, "Backend") and import App 1.0 in QML.
Don't: Copy Qt 6 QML_ELEMENT-annotated classes into a Qt 5 build.
Code Bad: class Backend : public QObject { Q_OBJECT QML_ELEMENT };  // Qt 6 only

Guideline: Expose list models as QAbstractListModel with roleNames
Description: A QAbstractListModel gives QML roles, change signals and lazy data; a QVariantList snapshot forces full reloads and loses updates.
Do: Implement roleNames() and data() and emit dataChanged for updates.
Don't: Push a QVariantList snapshot into a context property on every refresh.
Code Good: class DeviceModel : public QAbstractListModel { Q_OBJECT /* roleNames + dataChanged */ };
Code Bad: engine.rootContext()->setContextProperty("devices", variantList);  // snapshot

Guideline: Set object ownership explicitly for C++-owned QObjects
Description: Objects created in C++ and handed to QML default to C++ ownership, but ambiguity causes double-deletes or leaks when QML also parents them.
Do: Call QQmlEngine::setObjectOwnership(obj, QQmlEngine::CppOwnership) for C++-owned objects exposed to QML.
Don't: Let QML parent a C++-owned object and hope ownership sorts itself out.
Code Bad: /* object exposed with ownership left ambiguous */

Guideline: In Qt 5, Connections targets one object with onSignal handlers
Description: Qt 5 Connections uses target plus on<Signal> handlers; the Qt 6 function-handler form does not apply, and one Connections block serves exactly one target.
Do: Write one Connections block per signal source with onDataReady-style handlers.
Don't: Write Qt 6-style function handlers or one block for several targets in Qt 5.
Code Good: Connections { target: backend; onDataReady: list.model = data }  // Qt 5
Code Bad: Connections { function onDataReady(data) {} }  // Qt 6 form

Guideline: Minimum touch target 48 px, 60-72 px for gloved hands
Description: Small targets miss on touch panels; controlled environments (fixed-grip medical instruments, secured industrial panels) may justify smaller targets only after explicit safety review.
Do: Size tappable controls to at least 48 px (60-72 px gloved) using padding and implicit sizes.
Don't: Ship 32 px buttons on a touch panel.
Code Bad: Button { width: 32; height: 32 }  // un-tappable on touch

Guideline: No hover-only disclosure on touch panels
Description: Hover does not exist on touch; information or actions revealed only on hover are unreachable.
Do: Replace hover disclosure with explicit buttons or dedicated screens.
Don't: Hide the delete action behind a hover state.
Code Bad: MouseArea { hoverEnabled: true; onEntered: actions.visible = true }  // touch-dead

Guideline: Fixed pixel layout on fixed-resolution panels
Description: Fluid grids and breakpoints assume resizable windows; a fixed panel has one exact geometry and fluid layout wastes CPU re-negotiating it.
Do: Design to the panel's exact dimensions with fixed layout; reserve fluid layouts for desktop windows.
Don't: Run a fluid responsive grid on a 800x480 fixed panel.
Code Good: /* layout sized to the panel's exact 800x480 geometry */
Code Bad: /* breakpoints and fluid grid on a fixed panel */

Guideline: Every action needs a hardware-button fallback on panels
Description: Touch-only actions strand the operator when the touchscreen fails or gloves block input.
Do: Provide a hardware-key or button path for every action (Keys handling, FocusScope, KeyNavigation).
Don't: Leave critical actions reachable only by touch.
Code Bad: /* touch-only confirm, no key path */

Guideline: Alarms need three cues: color, shape and text
Description: Color alone fails under poor viewing angles, bright ambient light and color blindness; an alarm must survive all three.
Do: Pair every alarm with color plus an icon/shape plus a text label, and keep it persistent until acknowledged.
Don't: Signal an error with a red dot only.
Code Good: Row { Icon { name: "warning" } Text { text: qsTr("Pressure high") } }  // color + shape + text
Code Bad: Rectangle { color: "red" }  // color only

Guideline: Set Accessible.role and Accessible.name on custom controls
Description: Built-in Controls expose role and name automatically; custom items built from primitives are silent to screen readers without them.
Do: Add Accessible.role and Accessible.name to every custom interactive item.
Don't: Ship a custom switch built from Rectangle with no Accessible properties.
Code Bad: Rectangle { /* no Accessible properties */ }

Guideline: Mark decorative items Accessible.ignored
Description: Decorative dividers and ornaments read aloud as noise and bury the real content for screen-reader users.
Do: Set Accessible.ignored: true on purely decorative items.
Don't: Leave decorative images and dividers in the accessibility tree.
Code Bad: Image { /* decorative, but exposed to screen readers */ }

Guideline: Text contrast at least 4.5:1, 3:1 for large text and components
Description: Low contrast fails on bright panels and poor viewing angles; embedded screens are worse than desktop monitors.
Do: Check every text/background pair against 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text and UI components).
Don't: Ship light-grey body text on white because it looks clean.
Code Bad: Text { color: "#b0b0b0" }  // on white, fails

Guideline: Never use color alone to carry state
Description: Success, warning and error shown only by color are invisible to color-blind users and to monochrome displays.
Do: Pair every state color with an icon or text label.
Don't: Show error only by turning a border red.
Code Good: Row { Icon { name: "error" } Text { text: qsTr("Failed") } }
Code Bad: Rectangle { border.color: "red" }  // color only

Guideline: Use a modular type scale from a singleton, not ad-hoc sizes
Description: Ad-hoc pixel sizes drift into visual noise; a scale (base 16, ratio 1.333: caption 12, body 16, H2 21, H1 28, display 38) keeps at most three or four sizes per screen.
Do: Define TypeScale as a singleton (pragma Singleton + qmldir entry) and reference roles by name.
Don't: Sprinkle literal 11/13/15/17/19 px sizes across files.
Code Bad: Text { font.pixelSize: 13 }  // ad-hoc

Guideline: Prefer font.pointSize for body text, or derive from Screen.pixelDensity
Description: pixelSize ignores the OS font scale, so Large-font users get clipped layouts; pointSize respects platform DPI scaling.
Do: Use pointSize for body text, or size from a singleton driven by Screen.pixelDensity.
Don't: Hardcode pixelSize everywhere and ignore the OS font scale.
Code Bad: Text { font.pixelSize: 13 }  // ignores OS font scale

Guideline: Design containers for 30-40% text expansion
Description: Translated strings run 30-40% longer than English; fixed-width containers clip them.
Do: Let buttons and labels size implicitly and test with a long locale.
Don't: Fix button widths that clip translated labels.
Code Bad: Button { width: 80; text: qsTr("Save") }  // clips in translation

Guideline: Always set sourceSize on Image
Description: Without sourceSize, a large photo decodes at full resolution and burns memory on constrained devices.
Do: Set sourceSize to the displayed size (or the largest needed size).
Don't: Load a 4000 px photo into a 200 px thumbnail with no sourceSize.
Code Bad: Image { source: photo }  // full-resolution decode

Guideline: Load images asynchronously and check status
Description: Synchronous loads block the UI thread; assuming success leaves broken-image blanks with no fallback.
Do: Set asynchronous: true for network or large files and handle Image.Error via status.
Don't: Load remote or large images synchronously with no error path.
Code Good: Image { asynchronous: true; onStatusChanged: if (status === Image.Error) fallback() }
Code Bad: Image { source: remoteUrl }  // blocks, no error path

Guideline: Prefer SVG for icons, bitmaps for embedded GPU-less panels
Description: SVG scales without artifacts on desktop; on software-rasterised panels, bitmap icons pay raster cost at build time, not runtime.
Do: Use SVG icons on desktop; use pre-rasterised PNG icons on GPU-less embedded targets.
Don't: Ship vector paths that re-raster every frame on a GPU-less panel.
Code Bad: /* complex vector icon re-rastered per frame on soft raster */

Guideline: Avoid clip: true unless content genuinely overflows
Description: Clipping forces an offscreen render pass for the whole subtree; most clip flags are cargo-culted.
Do: Enable clip only where content must be masked, and keep the clipped subtree small.
Don't: Set clip: true on every container by habit.
Code Bad: Item { clip: true }  // on containers that never overflow

Guideline: Avoid opacity on complex subtrees; fade leaf colors instead
Description: Opacity on a subtree composites the whole subtree into a temporary surface before blending — very expensive.
Do: Animate color alpha on leaf items, or restructure so opacity is unnecessary.
Don't: Fade a whole screen subtree with opacity: 0.5.
Code Bad: Item { opacity: 0.5 }  // composites the whole subtree

Guideline: Use Item, not a transparent Rectangle, for invisible containers
Description: A plain Rectangle with no visible fill is still painted; Item costs only traversal.
Do: Use Item for hit-targets, containers and positioning anchors with no visible fill.
Don't: Wrap everything in Rectangle { color: "transparent" }.
Code Bad: Rectangle { color: "transparent" }  // still painted

Guideline: Use layer.enabled sparingly and disable it when idle
Description: layer.enabled rasterises the subtree into an FBO: it doubles memory for that branch and disables incremental rendering.
Do: Enable a layer only while an effect or cache genuinely requires it, and disable it when the effect is inactive.
Don't: Leave layer.enabled: true on static panels forever.
Code Bad: Item { layer.enabled: true }  // always, on a static panel

Guideline: Use role-based tokens, not raw hex values
Description: Token names should describe the role (surface, accent, error, outline), not the appearance (blue, grey-2); raw hex scatters the palette across files and kills dark mode.
Do: Define color tokens in a singleton and reference them by role everywhere.
Don't: Scatter "#2563eb" and "#f5f5f5" literals across components.
Code Bad: Rectangle { color: "#f5f5f5" }  // raw hex

Guideline: Never name a QML property on + capital letter
Description: on<Name> is reserved signal-handler syntax; a lone property color onPrimary may load today, but once the paired base token (primary) exists in the same object the component fails at load with 'Cannot assign a value to a signal'.
Do: Rename tokens consistently (textOnPrimary, primaryForeground, surfaceForeground).
Don't: Define property color onPrimary alongside property color primary in a theme singleton.
Code Bad: property color onPrimary: "#ffffff"  // load-time failure with primary present

Guideline: Design for light and dark themes from the start
Description: A token system handles dark mode automatically; hardcoded colors need a second pass over every file.
Do: Drive colors from the token singleton (or Material.theme) so a dark variant is a token swap, not a rewrite.
Don't: Hardcode light-theme colors and promise dark mode later.
Code Bad: /* every color hardcoded for light theme */

Guideline: Wrap every user-visible string in qsTr()
Description: Strings outside qsTr() never reach lupdate and ship untranslated; this includes text, placeholderText, title and tooltips.
Do: Wrap all user-visible strings; omit only internal identifiers and log messages.
Don't: Leave placeholderText or dialog titles as raw literals.
Code Bad: TextField { placeholderText: "Search" }  // untranslatable

Guideline: Use %1 placeholders, never concatenation
Description: Concatenation breaks translator reordering: word order differs across languages and concatenated fragments cannot be reordered.
Do: Write qsTr("Found %1 items").arg(count).
Don't: Build sentences with + string + concatenation.
Code Bad: qsTr("Found ") + count + qsTr(" items")  // untranslatable order

Guideline: Mirror layouts for RTL with LayoutMirroring, and check the leftovers
Description: For Arabic, Hebrew, Farsi and Urdu the whole layout mirrors; LayoutMirroring handles anchors and Layouts, but Text alignment, directional icons and manual x positions still need explicit attention.
Do: Set LayoutMirroring.enabled with childrenInherit near the root, mirror directional icons (Image.mirror), and use QLocale for dates and numbers.
Don't: Ship an LTR-only layout and flip only the text.
Code Good: LayoutMirroring { enabled: true; childrenInherit: true }  // root
Code Bad: /* LTR layout, Arabic text pasted in */

Guideline: Fix the device canvas size explicitly
Description: A fixed device screen (e.g. 1920x1080 exoscope) is one explicit canvas, not a resizable desktop window; sizing for a desktop window leaves the panel floating or letterboxed on the device.
Do: Set the window to the device's exact size and design to that geometry.
Don't: Size the UI for a resizable desktop window and hope it fits the panel.
Code Good: ApplicationWindow { width: 1920; height: 1080 }  // exact device canvas
Code Bad: ApplicationWindow { width: 1280; height: 720 }  // desktop size on a 1080p panel

Guideline: Put video first and controls in a fixed side panel
Description: For a camera device the live image is the work area; controls belong in a fixed panel that never covers it.
Do: Reserve the large area for video and dock controls in a fixed side panel.
Don't: Let control panels float over the live image or resize with it.
Code Good: RowLayout { VideoView { Layout.fillWidth: true } Panel { Layout.preferredWidth: 420 } }
Code Bad: /* panel overlays the video and hides the field of view */

Guideline: Give sliders a large handle and a live value readout
Description: A zoom/focus/light slider must be grabbable with gloves and its value readable at a glance; the default thin handle misses gloved fingers.
Do: Use a large custom handle, a stepSize, and a text readout bound to the value.
Don't: Ship the default thin slider with no value display on a touch panel.
Code Good: Slider { id: zoomSlider; stepSize: 0.2 } Text { text: zoomSlider.value.toFixed(1) }
Code Bad: Slider { }  // thin default handle, no readout

Guideline: Use a ToolBar header for the top bar
Description: ToolBar is the Controls 2 container for application-wide actions and is commonly used as an ApplicationWindow header.
Do: Put header actions in a ToolBar set as the window header.
Don't: Build the top bar from loose rectangles and buttons with manual layout.
Code Good: header: ToolBar { RowLayout { Button { text: qsTr("Back") } } }
Code Bad: Rectangle { /* hand-rolled header, no ToolBar semantics */ }

Guideline: Keep a compact control visibly selected
Description: Compact controls in a dense panel need an explicit selected/pressed state, or the operator cannot tell what is active.
Do: Use checked state plus a border or accent fill for the selected control.
Don't: Rely on subtle shade differences to show selection in a dense panel.
Code Good: Button { checkable: true; background: Rectangle { border.color: checked ? Theme.accent : "transparent" } }
Code Bad: Button { /* selected looks like everything else */ }

Guideline: Do not use Neumorphism on a surgical screen
Description: Soft low-contrast neumorphic shadows disappear under bright operating-room light and fail contrast on the panel.
Do: Use flat surfaces with a clear border and a strong pressed/checked state.
Don't: Style critical controls with soft same-color shadows and no border.
Code Good: Rectangle { color: Theme.surface; border.color: Theme.accent; border.width: 2 }  // flat + bordered
Code Bad: Rectangle { /* neumorphic: two soft shadows, no border, low contrast */ }

Guideline: Model device state as properties, not loose booleans in handlers
Description: Freeze, recording and light state must stay consistent across video, panel and status bar; state scattered in handlers drifts apart.
Do: Keep one property per device state on a single object and bind every view to it.
Don't: Track recording in a handler-local variable that the status bar never sees.
Code Good: property bool recording: false  // video, panel and status bar all bind to it
Code Bad: onClicked: { var rec = true }  // local, invisible to other views

Guideline: Show recording time and capture count as bound text
Description: An operator must see elapsed recording time and how many stills were taken without opening a menu.
Do: Bind a label to a timer-driven elapsed property and a photo counter property.
Don't: Hide recording time behind a menu or show it only after stopping.
Code Good: Text { text: fmtTime(recSeconds) } Text { text: qsTr("%1 photos").arg(photoCount) }
Code Bad: /* recording time only visible in a submenu */

Guideline: Bind, do not poll, for device values
Description: Property bindings update only when a value changes; a Timer poll re-runs work on a fixed schedule and wastes CPU on constrained hardware.
Do: Bind the readout to the device property and let the engine update it.
Don't: Poll a device value every 100 ms with a Timer to refresh a label.
Code Good: Text { text: device.temperature }  // binding updates on change
Code Bad: Timer { interval: 100; onTriggered: label.text = device.temperature }  // polling

Guideline: Render live video with VideoOutput, not a static image
Description: VideoOutput renders a MediaPlayer or Camera source; a static Image cannot show a live feed.
Do: Bind VideoOutput.source to the camera or player source and pick a fillMode.
Don't: Fake a live feed with a static Image updated from snapshots.
Code Bad: Image { source: "frame.jpg" }  // not a live feed

Guideline: Keep overlays off the clinical image unless they are the point
Description: Crosshairs and status strips are overlays; they must not hide the area the operator is working on.
Do: Keep overlays minimal, semi-transparent and parked at the edges; hide them when they are not the point.
Don't: Cover the center of the field with status panels and decorations.
Code Good: /* overlays: thin edge strips, opacity 0.7, center clear */
Code Bad: /* status panel covering the center of the image */

Guideline: Keep heavy work off the UI thread with WorkerScript
Description: Long work on the UI thread freezes touch input; WorkerScript runs JS in a separate thread and sends the result back.
Do: Offload heavy JS to a WorkerScript and update the UI from its message handler.
Don't: Run image analysis or large model processing inline in a button handler.
Code Bad: onClicked: { analyze(hugeModel) }  // blocks the UI thread

Guideline: Do not use emoji as icons
Description: Emoji render inconsistently across embedded fonts and carry no accessible name, so they fail both visually and for screen readers.
Do: Use an icon font or SVG image with a text label next to it.
Don't: Use an emoji character as the only affordance for an action.
Code Good: Row { Image { source: "save.svg" } Text { text: qsTr("Save") } }
Code Bad: Button { text: "💾" }  // emoji only, inconsistent + nameless

Guideline: Fall back to the system sans on embedded targets
Description: A named web font may not exist on an embedded device; QML then falls back silently and layout shifts.
Do: Name the preferred font but accept the system sans fallback, and verify layout with the fallback active.
Don't: Depend on a web font that is absent on the device and ship the shifted layout.
Code Good: Text { font.family: "Inter, sans-serif" }  // verified with fallback
Code Bad: Text { font.family: "SomeWebFont" }  // absent on device, silent shift

Guideline: Verify QML with qmlscene before shipping the panel
Description: A QML file that only looks right in an editor can fail at runtime on missing imports or bad bindings.
Do: Run qmlscene on the panel under the target Qt version before shipping, and fix every warning it prints.
Don't: Ship a panel that has never been loaded by the QML engine.
Code Good: qmlscene -I . main.qml  // clean run, no warnings
Code Bad: /* shipped straight from the editor, never loaded */
